statement_blocker: The repository supplies a problem-family label and theory gloss, not a proposition. It fixes no interval or endpoint convention, state space, differential equation or operator, coefficient and forcing regularity, boundary operators or data, solution concept, quantifier order, hypotheses, or conclusion. domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix the independent-variable interval and endpoints, scalar or state space and universes, equation or operator, coefficient and forcing domains, topology and norm structures, regularity, solution carrier, and all typeclass data.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not select existence, uniqueness, nonexistence, multiplicity, solvability, continuous dependence, a priori estimate, Green representation, spectral result, numerical convergence result, or a conjunction.

candidate_scope_not_credited: existence and uniqueness for a source-specific two-point nonlinear ODE boundary-value problem
a linear solvability criterion or Fredholm alternative with source-specific compatibility conditions

degenerate_cases_to_resolve: coincident or reversed endpoints and zero-length intervals
empty, singleton, or zero-dimensional state spaces
degenerate leading coefficients, singular endpoints, and discontinuous coefficients
homogeneous zero data, incompatible boundary data, resonance, and nontrivial homogeneous kernels
nonunique initial-value dynamics, finite-time blow-up, and weak versus classical solutions
separated versus coupled conditions and whether existence, uniqueness, or both range over every admissible datum
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1384 Sturm-Liouville theory, THM-M-1385 Sturm comparison, or THM-M-1386 Sturm separation

an initial-value Picard-Lindelof or Gronwall theorem presented as a two-endpoint solvability theorem
